title: Brick veneer at base of wall

checklist.item: Through-wall flashing at the base laps up the backup at least 8 in (200 mm), under the water barrier, and runs to the face of the veneer with a drip edge.
checklist.why: Flashing stopped short of the face lets water run back under the wall.

checklist.item: Weeps are shown directly on the flashing at 24 in (600 mm) centres or closer, with a mortar-dropping collection device in the cavity.
checklist.why: Blocked or missing weeps turn the cavity into a reservoir.

checklist.item: A clear drained air space of at least 1 in (25 mm) is shown behind the veneer.
checklist.why: The air space is the drainage plane and the pressure break.

checklist.item: Veneer ties and their spacing are shown, with corrosion-resistant material and embedment noted, per the masonry code in force.
checklist.why: Tie spacing is a code requirement and a structural one.

checklist.item: Continuous insulation in the cavity is uninterrupted at the base; the flashing does not short-circuit it more than necessary.
checklist.why: Slab edges and shelf angles are the usual thermal bridges.

checklist.item: Base of veneer sits at least 6 in (150 mm) above grade or 2 in (50 mm) above paving, and the movement joint below a shelf angle is dimensioned.
checklist.why: Brick near grade wicks water and spalls.
